title: Copper-carbon-nanotube composite conductors at scale
bottleneck: Copper-carbon-nanotube composites have demonstrated conductivity beyond pure copper in laboratory samples, promising lighter, more efficient wiring for motors, grids, and aerospace. But translating nanoscale interface quality to kilometer-scale wire has stalled: nanotube alignment, copper infiltration, and interfacial resistance degrade badly outside the lab.
why_it_blocks: Wiring is everywhere, and even single-digit percentage gains in conductivity compound into enormous energy savings across motors, transformers, and transmission. The physics works in a coupon; the manufacturing science to make a spool of it does not, so the grid keeps paying copper's resistive tax.
current_state: Lab demonstrations of ultra-conductive composites continue to advance, yet continuous wire-drawing processes that preserve the nanoscale architecture remain experimental. No commercial conductor product with verified beyond-copper performance exists.
